title: Capacitance Extraction via Machine Learning with Application to Interconnect Geometry Exploration
problem: Commercial parasitic extraction tools require 25+ minutes per process parameter change, bottlenecking design technology co-optimization (DTCO) workflows.
method: The approach trains a machine learning model on standard cell layouts—the repeating building blocks of chip designs—to predict capacitance, which measures how much electrical charge connections store. Once trained, this model predicts capacitance in milliseconds for new layouts, replacing commercial tools that require 25+ minutes per change. The predictions are as accurate as traditional 2.5D extraction methods (models that treat geometry as 2.5-dimensional), enabling designers to quickly test many design variations.
key_novelty: Machine learning predicts parasitic capacitance in milliseconds, enabling designers to rapidly test chip design parameter variations during optimization (tasks that previously required 25+ minutes each).
contributions: ML-based parasitic capacitance extraction from layout patterns
Millisecond prediction of coupling capacitance under unseen layer thickness
25-minute reduction to seconds for process parameter changes
Competitive error distribution vs state-of-the-art 2.5D extraction
primary_theme: ML-accelerated parasitic extraction for design technology co-optimization
